markdown.markdown:
In this lecture, we will explore the valorization of insect frass (i.e. the residual material from insect bioconversion processes) as a co-substrate for biomethane production. The session covers the intersection of circular economy principles, waste-to-energy systems, and sustainable bioprocessing technologies.

Key Topics: - Insect frass composition and characteristics relevant for biomethanization - Anaerobic co-digestion for enhanced biogas production - Process optimization strategies: Pretreatment methods, co-digestion with other organic substrates, retention time and temperature considerations - Current challenges and opportunities: Scale-up limitations, regulatory frameworks, integration with insect farming systems, economic potential

**Learning outcomes**: By the end of this lecture, you will have an understanding of how insect frass can be integrated into circular bioeconomy systems, be able to evaluate different bioprocessing technologies for frass valorization, and assess the feasibility of frass-based bioenergy production.
